submitted_prompt:
Edit Image 1, the eight-frame walking sheet. Repair ONLY the legs and supporting weight: all current frames repeat the same forward boot, so they do not walk. Image 2 is the original identity, adult proportions, lower-right camera, clothing and axe-hand reference.

Keep the same upper bodies, axe in the anatomical-right/screen-left hand, grid, scale and cell positions. In the TOP ROW, bring the leg that starts under the SCREEN-LEFT hip forward across the body toward LOWER-RIGHT: first cell has this leg extended in front, its boot is the forward/lower-right boot, while the other leg extends behind toward upper-left. In cells2 and3 this planted leg takes the weight and the other bent knee passes it; cell4 prepares the other leg's contact. In the BOTTOM ROW reverse the legs: the leg starting under the SCREEN-RIGHT hip plants forward while the screen-left hip's leg trails, then bends and passes forward into the top-left pose. The two contact silhouettes must visibly have opposite legs crossing in front, rather than identical legs with altered shading.

Eight ordered phases of one in-place walk, four columns by two rows. Retain the bone mask, dark topknot, charcoal-blue shoulder cloth, ochre sash, leather boots and broad bronze axe. Keep all heads and toes facing lower-right, constant body size and ground plane, with very small weight bob. Return crisp low-resolution pixel clusters with actual transparent alpha and no painted transparency checker.
